rule: partition every component into exact semantic-equivalence groups; singleton groups preserve distinct requirements

members.condition: when an attacker has complete control of the network
members.required_behavior: detect modifications to protected channel data
members.why_checkable: Active record-tampering tests can exercise the adjacent integrity property under the stated attacker model.

evidence.quote:
These properties should be true even in the face of an attacker who
   has complete control of the network, as described in [RFC3552].

members.condition: after the TLS channel is established
members.required_behavior: detect attacker modification of channel data
members.forbidden_behavior: accept modified protected data as authentic
members.why_checkable: Tampering with protected records can be tested to verify that modification is detected.

evidence.quote:
Integrity: Data sent over the channel after establishment cannot
      be modified by attackers without detection.

supporting_links.reason: Both impose the same check that modification of protected channel data is detected under an active network attacker; the canonical evidence directly states the integrity property.

members.required_behavior: list supported record-protection algorithm and HKDF-hash pairs
members.forbidden_behavior: advertise a pair the client does not support
members.why_checkable: The advertised pairs can be compared with the client's enabled cipher and hash implementations.

evidence.quote:
cipher_suites:  A list of the symmetric cipher options supported by
      the client, specifically the record protection algorithm
      (including secret key length) and a hash to be used with HKDF

members.condition: when a client offers cipher suites in ClientHello
members.required_behavior: use the list to indicate the AEAD algorithm and HKDF hash pairs supported by the client
members.forbidden_behavior: offer a cipher suite pair the client does not support
members.why_checkable: The offered cipher-suite pairs can be compared with the client's enabled AEAD and hash capabilities.

evidence.quote:
A list of cipher suites which indicates the AEAD algorithm/HKDF
      hash pairs which the client supports.

supporting_links.reason: Both require ClientHello.cipher_suites to list only supported record-protection/AEAD and HKDF-hash pairs. The canonical requirement is the clearer direct field definition.

members.required_behavior: send a supported_versions extension
members.why_checkable: Serialized ServerHello messages can be checked for the extension.

evidence.quote:
All implementations MUST send and use these extensions when offering
   applicable features:

   -  "supported_versions" is REQUIRED for all ClientHello, ServerHello,
      and HelloRetryRequest messages.

members.required_behavior: send supported_versions in the ServerHello
members.why_checkable: A TLS 1.3 ServerHello can be inspected for extension presence.

evidence.quote:
A server which negotiates TLS 1.3 MUST respond by sending
   a "supported_versions" extension

members.condition: the message is a TLS 1.3 ServerHello
members.required_behavior: include supported_versions
members.why_checkable: Every TLS 1.3 ServerHello extension list can be inspected for mandatory presence.

evidence.quote:
All TLS 1.3
      ServerHello messages MUST contain the "supported_versions"
      extension.

supporting_links.reason: Both require supported_versions in a TLS 1.3 ServerHello; the canonical is the clearer direct primary-body MUST statement with the negotiation condition explicit.

known_conflicts.reason: One member applies whenever sending a ServerHello, while the other applies only when the server negotiates TLS 1.3. The broader and narrower conditions are not equivalent even though both check for supported_versions.
